name: Xwela Gbe
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Hazoume, Marc-Laurent 1990. Etude comparative des parlers Gbe du Sud-Benin (comparative phonological study plausibly covering prosody; not online)

sources.citation: Henson, Bonnie J., Eric C. Johnson & Angela Kluge. 2011. A sociolinguistic survey of the Gbe language communities of Benin and Togo, Volume 4: Xwela language area. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2011-016. Dallas: SIL International. 43 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic survey (comprehension testing, attitudes, literacy); only remarks that villages report 'minor differences in tone'. Reference list contains no Xwela-specific phonological work (cites Capo 1986, 1991 for Gbe phonology).

sources.citation: Kluge, Angela. 2011. A sociolinguistic survey of the Gbe language communities of Benin and Togo: Gbe language family overview. SIL ESR 2011-012; Kluge 2007 (LDC 1) and Kluge 2008 (SIL ESR 2008-023) Gbe lexical/grammatical comparisons; Kluge 2005 Linguistic Discovery 3(1).
sources.note: Nothing on word stress; lexicostatistical comparisons in which 'length and tone' distinctions were disregarded. Xwela treated only for classification (western vs eastern Phla-Phera).

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0 inventory GM 1279 'xwela' (Xwela Gbe), source Capo 1991. https://phoible.org/inventories/view/1279
sources.note: Database entry: 45 segments incl. tones ˦ (H), ˨ (L), ˦˨ (HL); no stress information (second-hand from Capo 1991).
Gbe article: 'The Gbe languages are tonal languages' (H vs non-H tonemes, depressor consonants) — family-level, unsourced inline; nothing on stress; fr 'Xwela' gives only the CENALA alphabet.

sources.citation: Hazoume, Marc-Laurent. 1990. Étude comparative des parlers gbe du Sud-Bénin: Essai de classification synchronique. Cotonou: CENALA. 73 pp.; with Capo, H. B. C. 1990. Approche phonologique segmentale (same series, no. 3, 30 pp.).
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The Glottolog-listed CENALA comparative study (the earlier scan's named source); digitised at the IDRC Digital Library but restricted to IDRC staff — could be requested from IDRC (project 870102 'Langues nationales du Bénin').

sources.citation: Kinhou, Séverin-Marie. 2015. Éléments de lexicologie xwela. Cotonou: Christon Éditions / Les Éditions Ablɔɖè. 150 pp. ISBN 9789991903170.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Monograph on Xwela by the language's main Beninese specialist; blurb promises phonetic correspondences; likely contains an orthography/phonology chapter with tone (and any accent) conventions.

sources.citation: Gbéto, Flavien. 2004. Assimilation des pronoms objets des trois personnes du singulier en xwela, dialecte gbe du Bénin. Afrika und Übersee 87: 249-266.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Only published linguistic article devoted specifically to Xwela; Gbéto's Gbe papers always open with a phonological/tonal sketch of the lect, so a statement on tone (and possibly on the absence of stress) is likely.

sources.citation: Capo, Hounkpati B. C. 1991. A Comparative Phonology of Gbe (Publications in African Languages and Linguistics 14). Berlin/New York: Foris (de Gruyter reprint). Ch. 2 'Synchronic phonetic setting' (pp. 19-62).
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; library e-access not checked
sources.note: The primary phonological description covering Xwela (Phera) among all Gbe lects; ch. 2 gives each lect's inventory and the tone system and is the most likely place for an explicit statement that Gbe lects are tonal with no distinctive stress. Source of the PHOIBLE Xwela inventory.

sources.citation: Capo, Hounkpati B. C. 1988. Renaissance du gbe: réflexions critiques et constructives sur l'eve, le fon, le gen, l'aja, le gun, etc. Hamburg: Helmut Buske. (French original of the comparative phonology, with a chapter on tones.)
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Alternative to Capo 1991 with the same lect coverage (incl. Xwela/Phera) and an explicit discussion of Gbe prosody; HathiTrust search-only.

sources.citation: Hounzangbe, Marcellin Zinsou. n.d. Introduction à l'apprentissage de trois langues béninoises: le Xwlagbe de Grand-Popo, le Xwlagbe de Houlènou et le Xwelagbe des communautés xwla et xwela: cours d'initiation et préparation... (LoC record).
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Pedagogical primer for Xwla/Xwela; primers often state pronunciation rules including tone/accent conventions.

Xwela (Phera); PHOIBLE inventory GM 1279 derived from it lists Xwela tones H, L and HL — i.e. a tone system, no stress information.
